title: Review of the CIPS gene-selection negative finding on fresh seed 5: per-capita births of ancestors and mutants are equal (0.072 vs 0.074 per 1000 t), kinds stay pure (0 mixed, 0 label-less bodies), the trait arm holds fewer bodies; the mutant share is higher with the trait on this seed (0.78 vs 0.49), not through births
summary: Ran the fixed world.py and sel.py with a2 -0.1 (ancestors g2, inoc_kind 2, swap_T 100, wash_T 1000) and the a2 0 twin with the same streams on fresh seed 5 to t=25000, and a labkit pack of the trait arm (seed 5, 100 frames of 100 t). Mutant (g1) share over the last 5000 t 0.78 with the trait vs 0.49 in the twin (g2 share 0.22 vs 0.51); per-capita births per 1000 t ancestor/mutant 0.072/0.074 with the trait and 0.086/0.092 in the twin (5/4 and 9/6 counted births); 19 removals each; mean body count from t=6000 6.5 (5-11) vs 8.9 (7-11); 0 bodies with a mixed label (0.3-0.7) and 0 label-less bodies after t=2000 in either arm. labkit: 3 persistent splits, generation 1, 7 persistent tracks.

observations.H: rates.out: births per body per 1000 t, ancestor g2 / mutant g1, 0.072/0.074 (a2 -0.1) and 0.086/0.092 (a2 0): no birth-rate advantage for the mutant, as the finding says. ana_s5.png: the g2 share tracks the twin to t~15000 and then falls to 0.15-0.3 with the trait against 0.45-0.65 in the twin (mean last 5000 t 0.22 vs 0.51), with 9 vs 10 g2 bodies among the 19 removals; the population with the trait sinks to 5-7 bodies while the twin keeps 8-11. Kind purity: 0 mixed and 0 label-less body records in both arms.

seeds_run.result: pass for the birth-rate negative and for purity; the share differs between arms (mutants 0.78 vs 0.49), in the selective direction, with equal per-capita births

controls_run.H: sel2_s5_a0.0.json: a2 0 twin, same seed, washout and swap streams

verdicts.limitation: Very small numbers: 4-9 counted births per kind per run and ~50 intervals skipped by rates.py, so per-capita rates are rough; the share difference on this seed arises after t=15000 when the trait population falls to 5-7 bodies, where a single removal moves the share by 0.15. With the author's seeds the mutant share is higher with the trait on 2 of 3 seeds (0.71, 0.40, now 0.78 vs 0.37, 0.73, 0.49), so 'not consistent' stands, but the sign test is far from decided. The trait arm carries fewer bodies than its twin again (6.5 vs 8.9), as on all the author's pairs.
